title: Lazy slice loading: corrupt bodies, misnamed files and moved files
findings_note: s312 relay 2026-10-17: done/remove/start/park now succeed on an item whose slice body is corrupt; a lookup by an id that lives only in a misnamed file misses before a full load; a State held across an external move raises a raw FileNotFoundError
boundary: **Not in this slice:** reverting lazy loading (owner decision (a), 2026-10-16).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
s312 loads slice bodies on first access. Three behaviours changed or appeared:
- `done`, `remove`, `start` and `park` now succeed on an item whose slice body is corrupt; before s312 the whole load refused. ARCHITECTURE.md says so; the CHANGELOG does not name those commands.
- Before a full load, an id that lives only inside a misnamed slice file (its stem differs) is not found. `verify` still reports the file.
- A State held across an external move of a slice file gets a raw `FileNotFoundError` from `jsonio.read`, not `corrupt`.
The first two are trade-offs the owner has to accept or reverse; the third is a bug.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/store.py` (lazy read path), `src/slicer/jsonio.py` if the error is mapped there; `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `tests/test_store_lazy.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_LazyBody_FileMovedAfterLoad_ReportsCorrupt` (or `io`, as the owner decides).
- Owner-dependent: `test_Done_CorruptBody_Refuses` if the owner wants the old refusal back for mutating commands.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Wait for the owner's answers on the first two points (flagged needs-owner).
2. Map the missing file to a SlicerError with a stable code.
3. Name the affected commands in the CHANGELOG entry.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
